payload.explanation:
u_brown did not end seated at u_brown_placement when place_u_brown closed. I checked this against TF, not the executor's claim. The placement frame moves with base1, so I measured against its current pose. The final u_brown pose (0.4029, -0.1442, 0.0575) is 0.0136 m from u_brown_placement (0.3968, -0.1436, 0.0454), over the 0.01 m position_m tolerance. Most of that error is +0.012 m in z, so the part is sitting high. Its orientation is 26.4 deg off, over the 10 deg tolerance.

What physically happened: the object_poses and tcp frames over the step show u_brown tracking the tcp exactly through the descent until about wall_ns 1792978905.4e9. Then, while the gripper was still closed, the part stopped descending with the tcp. Its offset in the tcp frame shrank by about 0.013 m in z and it tilted about 26 deg (quaternion y/z components went from about 0 to 0.13-0.15). Over the same moment, finger_joint effort dropped from 60.7 to 39.7. The tcp kept descending to z 0.1327. This pattern is the part jamming on the base1 fixture during insertion and being levered over inside the fingers. The contact pushed base1 by about 0.010 m and yawed it about 1.1 deg, which is within disturbance_tolerance_m 0.02, so it is reported but not counted as a base1 violation. The gripper then released the part where it lay: tilted, resting on the slot edge about 12 mm above its seat. The positional in-hand shift (about 0.015 m) stayed under grasp_slip_tolerance_m 0.02, so I don't count it as a slip violation. The rotation in hand is the mechanism of the misseat.

Grasp-phase clauses held: lift 0.1996 m, effort plateau 57.98, peak effort 61.3 against a limit of 100. Grasp width could not be observed independently; see the clause note. The executor also claimed failure, so the two records agree. The executor has begun an unplanned recovery step, reseat_pick_u_brown, which is not on the expected process. Frames of the descent were captured under label place_u_brown_descent_misseat.

payload.explanation:
u_orange moved relative to the gripper while it was still held, during place_approach_u_orange. The executor claimed success for this step.

Evidence: object_poses for u_orange paired with the tcp frame. u_orange tracked the tcp exactly from the grasp through wall_ns ~1792979183.27e9, with its tcp-frame offset constant at (-0.0004, -0.0253, 0.0873). In the next 0.5 s the part stopped following the tcp. The offset jumped 0.024 m, which fired slip_u_orange (limit grasp_slip_tolerance_m 0.02). It settled about 0.036 m from the grasp offset, with u_orange tilted ~15 deg (quaternion y/z went from ~0 to -0.08/-0.10). finger_joint never opened, so this is not a release.

Mechanism: this step's move_grasp_center_to_pose skill was commanded straight to the u_orange_placement seat pose (grasp centre z 0.045, no standoff target_offset). The tcp therefore travelled a single diagonal line from (0.70, -0.35, 0.33) down onto the seat, instead of staging above the slot and descending vertically. u_orange's centre was at about z 0.075 while still ~0.027 m +x of the slot. It struck the base1 fixture's top or slot rim and was shoved up into the fingers and rotated as the arm kept driving.

Corroborating evidence afterwards: arm joint efforts were very large while stationary (shoulder_lift 451, elbow 551, wrist_1 220), meaning the arm is still loaded against the obstruction. finger_joint effort rose to 105.7, still under u_orange's 200 limit. base1 was pushed again: it is now 0.0128 m from its run-start pose and yawed ~3.4 deg cumulatively, still within disturbance_tolerance_m 0.02. Seated u_brown moved ~0.0025 m along with base1.

u_orange now rests wedged 0.028 m above and ~0.027 m +x of u_orange_placement. Its seating will be judged when place_u_orange closes. Frames were captured under label place_approach_u_orange_slip.

payload.explanation:
The base1 fixture was physically disturbed during reseat_pick_u_orange. This step is NOT on the expected process; it is the executor's unplanned retry of the failed place_u_orange.

Evidence: base1's object_poses sampled at 20 Hz. base1 was static at (0.39221, -0.19150, 0.02237) through the approach. When the gripper closed on u_orange, which was leaning wedged in base1's slot at ~54 deg, base1 began to roll slightly (qx 0.0018, z +0.0002). During the lift, between wall_ns 1792979322.52e9 and 1792979323.42e9, base1 was hauled with the part: z rose from 0.0224 to 0.0332 (11 mm off the bench), roll reached ~7 deg (qx -0.062), and it was dragged +0.0153 m in y. The wedged part then broke free and base1 dropped back flat at (0.39221, -0.18596).

The still_bystanders_base1 monitor measures from base1's run-start pose, because no step is permitted to move the fixture. It fired at 0.0211 m against disturbance_tolerance_m 0.02. base1's resting displacement is now 0.0165 m from run start with ~3.2 deg of yaw. That displacement accumulated over four part-on-fixture contacts: about 0.010 m in place_u_brown, ~0.012 m after reseat_pick_u_brown, 0.0127 m after place_u_orange, and 0.0165 m now. Measured only from where base1 last rested before this step, the drag was 0.0136 m at peak and 0.0055 m at rest. I judge this non_conformant anyway: the fixture was lifted off the bench and dropped, and its cumulative departure from its original pose crossed the registry bound. Both measures are stated so a reviewer can weigh them.

Mechanism: the misseated u_orange was jammed in the slot. Re-grasping and lifting it straight up pulled the fixture with it until the part tore free. This is part-on-fixture contact, not an arm strike. The placement frames are attached to base1, so seated u_brown moved with it (0.0011 m from its frame now, still seated). The bystanders were checked at re-arm time and have not moved (still within 0.1 mm of run start). Frames were captured under label reseat_pick_u_orange_base1_displaced.

payload.explanation:
The base1 fixture was shoved about 0.029 m across the bench during place_inverted_u_yellow. base1 is not among this step's object_ids and is never to be displaced. That exceeds disturbance_tolerance_m 0.02 by every measure: 0.0289 m from where it stood at step start, 0.0304 m from its last rest pose, 0.0286 m from its run-start pose.

Evidence: object_poses for base1, the parts and the tcp at 20 Hz. The tcp descended vertically at x 0.392, y -0.187. It carried inverted_u_yellow (an inverted U meant to straddle line_green between u_brown and u_orange) down from z 0.124. At wall_ns ~1792979695.4e9, with the part's centre at z 0.091 (about 47 mm above its seat), the seated parts began to tilt: line_green to qy 0.22 (~26 deg), u_brown and u_orange a few degrees. By 1792979696.67e9, base1 and all three seated parts had jumped together ~0.016-0.021 m in -y while the descending part stayed at y -0.183. The fixture continued to slide over the next few seconds to (0.3780, -0.2128).

Mechanism: the inverted U came down onto the tops of the already-seated parts, most likely line_green's raised bar, rather than into the gap over them. The vertical press was converted into a lateral shove that slid the whole fixture assembly across the bench. This is part-on-part/fixture contact by the carried part, not an arm strike. Because the placement frames ride on base1, u_brown, u_orange and line_green are each still within 0.0025-0.0066 m of their placement frames, so their seating relative to the fixture survived. The fixture's position on the bench did not.

Monitor fires on u_brown (0.024), line_green (0.029) and u_orange (0.023) during this step were NOT adjudicated as findings. This step names all three in object_ids, so the undisturbed-objects invariant my per-part monitors enforced did not govern them here. Those monitors were mis-scoped for this step. The parts' requirement is their seating, which held. The executor's claim for this step is not yet available because end_step has not arrived. Frames were captured under label place_inverted_u_yellow_knock.

- u_orange: 0.0025 m and ~0.1 deg, within 0.02. Seated.

Timeline, and what became of each finding:
1. place_u_brown: u_brown misseated (0.0136 m, 26.4 deg). It jammed on base1 during the descent and was levered over in the fingers. The executor ran the unplanned steps reseat_pick_u_brown and reseat_place_u_brown, which are not on the expected process. u_brown ended 0.0019 m / 1.7 deg off, so this finding was CORRECTED.
2. place_approach_u_orange: in-hand slip of 0.0358 m while held, which fired slip_u_orange. The approach drove diagonally straight to the seat pose, and the part struck base1's rim.
3. place_u_orange: u_orange left leaning at 53.9 deg. The executor ran the unplanned reseat_pick_u_orange and reseat_place_u_orange. u_orange ended 0.0024 m / 0.4 deg off, CORRECTED.

6. place_inverted_u_yellow milestone: the part itself is misseated (0.0213 m, 16.7 deg). NOT corrected; the executor aborted.
